title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration

details.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
details.abstract: Hi everyone! 👋 I'm the first author of this paper. TL;DR: We ask what is actually redundant at high resolution in multi-scale all-in-one image restoration (AIO-IR) networks, and use the answer to build HiGLR , a fast and memory-efficient AIO-IR model. Our stage-wise analysis finds three redundancies, and each one leads to a design choice: Finest stage: what self-attention adds beyond uniform pooling is largely shared across queries → we replace it with a learned, input-independent kernel. Intermediate stages: neighboring queries select largely the same keys → Block-Routed Hybrid Attention (BRHA) shares routing indices across neighbors and combines coarse dense attention over block summaries with fine block-sparse attention over value residuals. ConvFFNs: spatial mixing tolerates much lower rank than the nonlinear expansion → Dual-Space FFN (DSFFN) does spatial mixing in a compact space and keeps the expanded part pointwise, enabling kernel fusion. With only 7M parameters, HiGLR achieves state-of-the-art results on AIO-3, AIO-5 and CDD-11, with up to 4.24× faster inference and 65.8% lower peak GPU memory than CEA-IR-S. Our approach learns preferences over individual parts while retaining geometric supervision, without changing the generator’s architecture. We explore both how to build useful preference pairs and how to balance preference optimization with reconstruction. Pair quality and coverage matter—not simply adding more pairs. title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures

details.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
details.abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or failed pickup with ground-truth object pose, contact, and surface points. WorldReforge turns this ground truth into two training signals without additional inference cost. Interaction Alignment focuses reconstruction on the small object and contact regions that a global loss underweights, and Surface Correspondence trains backbone features to follow the same physical surface points across frames. On Cosmos3 Nano, WorldReforge reduces object trajectory error by 28.2% overall and by 35.0% on unseen objects, and it lowers the error in predicting how two actions' outcomes diverge by 43.3%. Although trained only in simulation, it also improves reconstruction on DROID and on real failure videos. Controlled data studies show that failed contact and successful holding teach complementary physics: failed contact teaches how objects respond, and holding teaches how a grasped state persists. Our code, data, and models are available at https://github.com/aim-uofa/WorldReforge .

title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time

details.title: Beyond Self-Consistency: Recursive Self-Improvement at Test Time
details.abstract: Most test-time methods for LLMs vote : sample independent answers and trust the majority, both to pick the final answer and to build training targets. That wastes earlier reasoning, and when the majority is wrong, training on it reinforces the error. TT-RSI (Test-Time Recursive Self-Improvement) lets the model build on its own previous attempts instead, with no labels: In-Context RSI (inference, training-free): re-solve each question with the full previous solution as a neutral reference; the model decides what to reuse, rework, or redo. In-Weight RSI (label-free test-time training): distills successive refinements into the weights via on-policy self-distillation (Recursive + Accelerated Distillation). Because it learns from refinement rather than agreement, it can move past a wrong majority. The two reinforce each other: the updated model refines better, producing stronger references for the next round. We also show that distilling just two successive solutions moves the first attempt toward the model's infinite-step refinement limit. Results : +13.89% average accuracy over the base model, and +4.79% over TTPO + SC, the strongest self-consistency method, at the same test-time budget. 🌐 Project page: https://uanu2002.github.io/TT-RSI/ 💻 Repo: https://github.com/uanu2002/TT-RSI

title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification

details.title: ROAM-Bench: Evaluating Embodied Active Spatial Intelligence through Evidence Verification
details.abstract: Introducing ROAM-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating embodied active spatial intelligence through evidence verification! As illustrated in the teaser, counting mugs can require exploring multiple rooms and opening closed storage. We check both the final outcome and whether the agent completes the required observations and interactions, with additional checks of geometry and object placement. ROAM-Bench includes 250 manually validated tasks across 27 indoor environments, covering five groups of spatial abilities. Evaluating seven frontier vision-language models alongside humans reveals two complementary failures: correct outcomes with unmet exploration or interaction requirements, and incorrect judgments even after stronger verification checks pass. These findings help identify where exploration, spatial reasoning, and action fail to work together. 🌐 Project page: https://rxjfighting.github.io/ROAM-Bench/ ⭐ Code and tasks: https://github.com/rxjfighting/ROAM-Bench 🤗 Scene assets: https://huggingface.co/datasets/xjran/ROAM-Bench-scenes Feedback and discussion are welcome!

title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations

details.title: Beyond Code and Pixels: Co-Generating Editable and Visually Rich Presentations
details.abstract: Generating PPTX presentations is a structured task that requires semantic planning, visual composition, precise layout, and editability, motivating collaboration among specialized agents. However, programmatic methods offer editability but often produce rigid designs, while image-based methods provide visual richness but flatten content into difficult-to-edit pixels. A hybrid system can combine these strengths, but must coordinate interdependent decisions across content, layout, and appearance. To address this challenge, we propose SlidesWeaver, a hybrid multi-agent system that coordinates language and vision agents through shared deck- and slide-level states. Specifically, it uses staged multimodal commitment, diffusion-based composition planning, and two generation schedules for different priorities between composition freedom and accurate text preservation, while preserving native text and geometry. Across 1,728 generations spanning 24 system-model configurations, SlidesWeaver achieves consistently superior overall quality across all evaluated dimensions while maintaining structural control, editability, and practical generation efficiency.

title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation

details.title: SEEK: Self-Evolution through Execution Knowledge for Agentic Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: General-purpose multimodal foundation models enable robots to adapt during deployment from observations and execution feedback, without task-specific demonstrations or training. However, the robot retains what it learns only in the model's working context. Once the task ends, it loses this execution knowledge, such as how to carry a bowl between two grippers. On the next attempt at the task, the robot may take just as long and repeat the same mistakes. To avoid this repetition, robots must retain execution knowledge across attempts. Yet replaying past actions is insufficient, because their effects depend on the current conditions. Procedures that determine actions from the current scene address this, but when they meet conditions that earlier attempts did not cover, revising them requires the measured effects of earlier actions. We therefore propose SEEK, an agentic framework that retains both, enabling robots to improve across attempts while keeping the underlying model fixed. To adapt retained knowledge to the current scene, SEEK adopts a Self-Evolving Programmatic Policy (SEPP) that encodes manipulation as executable procedures and determines each action from current observations. As the robot executes these procedures, SEEK records the measured effects of its actions, including those from failed attempts, in a Persistent Action-Effect Bank (PAEB). Where a retained procedure applies, it acts without a model request; where it meets a condition it does not cover, this evidence guides its revision. On RoboDojo, knowledge retained over ten attempts raises SEEK's average task score from 27.0 to 54.4 and its success rate from 19.7% to 48.0% across all 42 tasks. On 34 of these tasks with GPT-6.2 Astra, SEEK reaches 80.1 after five attempts, against 49.6 for the same model acting directly, and uses 77.6% fewer model requests.

title: RoboEvo^2: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution

details.title: RoboEvo^2: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
details.abstract: Introducing RoboEvo² , a framework in which a robot's policy and its coding-agent harness improve each other. Policy failures tell the coding agent what to repair; verified repairs become reusable agent skills and new policy training data. Over rounds, the policy succeeds more on its own and the agent is called less, with no new human demonstrations. Project page | Paper · Code · Model weights Harness–policy co-evolution Policy → Harness (P2H): for each policy failure, a VLM coding agent searches Code, Code+ICL and Code+Policy repairs in parallel and merges verified solutions into reusable skills, memory and routing. Harness → Policy (H2P): verified trajectories train the policy, and Counterfactual Preference Distillation (CPD) teaches it to prefer the successful correction over the failure from the same starting state. Results: on LIBERO-PRO, standalone policy success rises from 11.0% to 84.1% and hybrid success from 30.4% to 90.5% over eight rounds, while the agent's API cost per round falls by 77%. On the Unitree G1-D, hybrid success reaches 95.0%.

title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents

details.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
details.abstract: We present Loupe, an agentic framework for knowledge-intensive video generation that addresses the challenges of missing factual knowledge, entity appearances, and temporal relationships in user prompts. Loupe autonomously leverages text search, image search, and web browsing to retrieve, verify, and integrate external evidence, producing factually grounded video prompts and visual references for downstream video generators. To enable effective agent training, we introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), a process supervision framework that derives task-specific evaluation criteria directly from user requests and provides fine-grained, step-level feedback for search and planning decisions. Building on RBC, we develop RBC-SFT and RBC-GRPO, enabling effective supervised and reinforcement learning without requiring video rendering during training. We also introduce Search-VBench, a dedicated benchmark consisting of 150 prompts across seven categories for evaluating knowledge-intensive video generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate consistent improvements across multiple video generators, increasing MiniMax-H3's overall score from 32.80 to 70.67, highlighting the effectiveness of search augmentation and process supervision for knowledge-intensive video generation.

title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand

details.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand

This opens a new co-design frontier: models trained to manage their own context, served by inference engines that support KV cache editing.

title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents

details.title: Demystifying the Autoresearch Harness: How Context and Skills Shape Self-Evolving Agents
details.abstract: What actually drives long-horizon, self-evolving autoresearch agents? This paper systematically demystifies agent harness design across context and skill management on MLE-Bench and KernelBench. Rather than rolling summaries or complex skill consolidation, the authors reveal that simple mechanisms such as context folding (expandable per-attempt digests, up to +19.2%) and skill deletion (pruning unused lessons) deliver the strongest gains. Combining these principles in MLEvolver dramatically outperforms AIDE and OpenEvolve under the same budget, achieving a 45.5% gold medal rate (+42.9% over baselines) on MLE-Bench Lite and 62% fast₂ on KernelBench Level 3 (over 2× AIDE and 4× OpenEvolve).

Visuomotor policies trained on our data, such as GR00T N1.7, work both in simulation and on a real robot. title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift

details.title: When Does Reasoning Help Entity Disambiguation? Small LLMs In-Domain and Under Shift
details.abstract: Entity disambiguation (mapping ambiguous mentions in text to entities in a knowledge base) is a foundational step in tasks such as knowledge graph construction, question answering, and information extraction. Recent work has applied LLMs to this problem, achieving stateof-the-art performance. Notably, reasoning LLMs have been shown to perform entity disambiguation in a true zero-shot fashion, generalizing across knowledge bases and domains. However, it is unclear whether this capability survives, or remains competitive, with smaller LLMs, where entity disambiguation has typically relied on reranking rather than reasoning. We ask when reasoning is worth its cost at small scale. We compare pointwise, listwise, and reasoning-based candidate-selection components within a classical coarse-to-fine entity disambiguation pipeline, across the classical, few-shot and true zero-shot settings. The reasoning paradigm is trained with distillation and reinforcement learning recipes. The benefit of reasoning grows with domain shift: negligible in-domain, decisive in the true zero-shot setting. We show that two distinct factors are at work: the reranker's uncertainty over the candidates locates where the paradigms disagree, while shift governs which is right when they do.

title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation

details.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
details.abstract: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guarantee. For multi-turn conversations, Lembas reuses the tokens processed in earlier turns and refines relevance with the VLM's attention at no extra cost. Our evaluations show that Lembas improves accuracy by up to 7.2 percentage points over state-of-the-art baselines at comparable compute. On multi-turn video understanding, Lembas achieves up to 1.5 percentage points higher accuracy with 1.7-17.3x fewer TFLOPs.

title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents

details.title: Evaluation-Free Recursive Self-Improvement for Coding Agents
details.abstract: 🚀 Can coding agents recursively improve themselves without evaluating candidate agents on downstream tasks? We introduce ELITE (Explore-then-Integrate) , a new approach to recursive self-improvement that shifts from evaluation-driven candidate selection to compatibility-aware mechanism integration. Instead of repeatedly benchmarking evolved agents to select the next parent, ELITE explores diverse self-modifications from a shared parent and combines complementary implementation mechanisms into a single descendant. Key results: 60.0% → 85.6% on SWE-bench Pro. Zero downstream candidate task evaluations during evolution. 8.8× and 3.2× faster evolution than DGM and HGM, respectively, under the evaluated configurations. Strong cross-benchmark transfer without further adaptation: 73.3% on SWE-bench Verified and 69.3% on Polyglot . Our findings suggest that downstream evaluation need not be an intrinsic component of recursive self-improvement, opening up new possibilities for efficient and transferable self-improving agents. 📄 Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.21056 We welcome feedback and discussion from the community!

title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models

details.title: Lost in Translation, Not in Confidence: Benchmarking and Calibrating Multilingual Decision Models
details.abstract: Decision models are language models finetuned to return a probability for each option of a typed query, which routers and guardrails threshold directly. They are built on multilingual bases but ranked almost entirely in English. We evaluate 25 top-ranked open-weight decision models on 17 tasks in 14 languages, comparing each language with English on parallel items. Every model loses accuracy in every language, from about 2 points in highresource languages to 8 in Tamil, while confidence falls only half as much: a threshold set for 95% accuracy in English yields 90% in Tamil. The size of the loss is set by the language and the base model rather than by leaderboard rank. In 81 controlled fine-tuning runs, task skill learned in English transfers to other languages and a few thousand target-language items narrow large losses, but neither more data nor full-parameter tuning closes them. Finally, the same test items are answered more accurately in all 23 benchmark–language pairs we compare when an LLM rather than a person translated them, so LLM-translated test sets understate the gap.

title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation

details.title: SPARC: Geometry-Guided Attention Pruning for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation
details.abstract: We present SPARC, a geometry-guided attention pruning framework that turns the native self-attention of pretrained video diffusion transformers into a unified mechanism for camera control and persistent scene memory. Our key insight is that attention connectivity can simultaneously serve as geometric conditioning for camera control and spatial addressing for historical memory retrieval. Motivated by the asymmetric contextual requirements of reconstructing observed content and synthesizing novel regions, SPARC restricts observed tokens to geometrically corresponding historical tokens and local spatiotemporal context, while preserving dense attention for unobserved regions. Correspondence-aware attention biasing and order-invariant historical positioning further enable stable retrieval across long temporal gaps. Without introducing additional learnable control or memory modules, SPARC achieves precise camera adherence and faithful scene revisitation while substantially reducing attention computation. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of aggressive attention pruning in improving camera adherence, revisit consistency, and visual fidelity, with an inference speedup of over 50x when combined with four-step distillation.

title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards

details.title: Negative-Only Policy Optimization for One-Sided Verifiable Rewards
details.abstract: NeurIPS 2026 Spotlight A failed unit test tells us a program is wrong. Passing a few tests still leaves its correctness uncertain. Can we train a policy using only the failures we trust? We introduce Negative-Only Policy Optimization (NOPO), which lowers the probability of verified failures and treats the remaining responses as unlabeled. Across coding, logic, and math benchmarks, NOPO improves pass@k when training relies on incomplete checks.

title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator

details.title: SOLVE: Sparse, Ordered Keyposes Make LLM Agents Versatile and Efficient Robot Manipulator
details.abstract: LLM agents have made remarkable progress in robot manipulation, yet they suffer from expensive inference, dense step-by-step control, and tool bottlenecks. We introduce SOLVE, a training-free, versatile and efficient agent policy: a multimodal LLM agent writes a sparse, ordered sequence of 6-DoF end-effector keyposes per call, observes the result, and writes the next, while a motion planner interpolates between them. The agent decides the number and spacing of keyposes for both fast long-range motion and fine-grained manipulation. This granularity matches the sparsity of teleoperated manipulation: most demonstrations in DROID can be compressed into a few keyposes instead of dense actions. SOLVE grounds keyposes with sparse depth queries answered by noisy sources, such as multi-view triangulation, stereo, or monocular depth, and copes with that noise itself. It also improves from execution feedback, reflecting on its own rollouts and distilling a few rules per task. SOLVE reaches state-of-the-art performance of 74.5% on RoboDojo and 84.5% on RoboLab, with only $1.7 per episode on average, 12x less than previous dense-control agent policies. On a real robot, the same agent achieves an 88% success rate (75 of 85 episodes) over 16 challenging zero-shot tasks. Our project page is at https://serenos.github.io/solve-website .

title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability

details.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
details.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose Stable GDN-2, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an O(√T) upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that Stable GDN-2 achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models

details.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
details.abstract: A foundation model for time series is pre-trained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. Such datasets are scarce, and a few public leaderboards carry most comparisons, yet none of them states how small a difference its datasets can detect. We call that quantity the resolution of a board and introduce Vernier , a tool that computes it from the files a board already publishes. Vernier also reports which entries a board cannot separate from its leader and whether its order changes when unrelated parties submit. GIFT-Eval resolves 6.8 rank places, and its displayed neighbours sit 0.91 apart. The ten places of its top ten hold fewer than two resolvable steps. fev-bench, Chronos Benchmark II and TIME show the same pattern: their resolution is 3.6 to 19 times the gap between neighbours. With each of its 2,554 series as an independent source, BOOM is the one board that resolves its top ten. Below the resolution the order depends on who else submitted: across four boards, rules that rank against the pool reversed 43 top-ten pairs with neither entry rerun, in one update in seven. Boards also do not record how much history a model receives. On 70 configurations, shortening it raised the error of three of four open models, two of them by 15%. We release Vernier, which runs this report with one command on any leaderboard that publishes per-dataset scores: https://github.com/therealram18/vernier

title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation

details.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
details.abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. We evaluate five video generators using verified, case-specific checklists. Experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but greater proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, while strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding.

title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models

details.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
details.abstract: Same first frame, same prompt, same evaluator: instead of generating pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video. On VBVR-Pro-Bench, Codex, Claude Code and Gemini CLI score 0.92 / 0.89 / 0.89, more than 0.22 above the strongest video model. Program synthesis is currently the more reliable route to visual reasoning.

title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation

details.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
details.abstract: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes. Confirmed generation results are linked to the corresponding asset states, story time, and reference versions for verification and reuse by subsequent shots. Hierarchical Collaboration isolates execution contexts by task, clip, and repair round, and uses hierarchical memory to organize this process across multiple sets. Across multiple benchmarks, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods and produces long videos with sustained cross-shot consistency under predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.

title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents

details.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
details.abstract: How much of the relevant knowledge does a deep research agent actually cover? We built DRBench Pro to answer this question. For each case, we derive a research query and evidence-grounded rubrics from the same Wikipedia-derived knowledge tree. This structure lets us measure breadth across major research directions and depth along related chains of knowledge. DRBench Pro includes 144 research cases across 24 domains and 44,102 rubrics . In our evaluation of 16 agent configurations, we found that similar overall coverage scores can mask distinct strengths in breadth and depth. If you evaluate your own agent with DRBench Pro, we'd love to see your results and hear what you think. Project & leaderboard · Code · Dataset

title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation

details.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: TL;DR: When a multimodal LLM agent calls a learned visuomotor policy (e.g., a VLA), the system often fails at the handoff : the agent invokes the policy from states where the policy is not reliable. We call the region where the policy is reliable its handoff boundary , and propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning . It shapes this boundary through training instead of leaving the agent to guess where it lies. Boundary-Explicit Training: fine-tune the policy only on contact segments, starting from diverse poses. This makes the boundary wide and simple enough to describe to the agent in a short handoff protocol. Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement: curate the system's own successful rollouts and retrain the policy on them. This extends the boundary to earlier task stages, so the agent hands over sooner and makes fewer LLM calls. Results 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, +26.4 points over the strongest baseline; 69.2% on RoboDojo, +28.4 points. Self-improvement cuts API cost by 41.3% and execution time by 37.5% on average, with no drop in success. 91.1% of the agent's first handoffs land within 40 mm of the policy's training trajectories. title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?

details.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
details.abstract: We gave a minimal tool-calling agent database tasks with hazards in them (free up disk space, clean up tables, an instruction injected into the data, a superuser password left in an application table) and ran six small open-weight models against nine engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, ClickHouse, Cassandra, MongoDB, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch. 9,468 trials, preregistered. Some results: Under least privilege, agents used the planted superuser password in 24 of 4,032 trials, all but one after the engine had refused their own account. Out of the box, in 215 of 392 trials that lost data, the only thing lost was a backup copy the agent could reach. The engine mattered most in what it lets you undo. Cassandra's default snapshot before TRUNCATE and DROP undid every such loss (0 of 432 trials). Model choice moved loss about as much as engine choice: 3.0% to 16.8% out of the box. Three of the seven preregistered hypotheses met their decision rule. Every trial record, with per-turn model reasoning, is on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24445015

title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers

details.title: Revisiting LLMs as Context Engineers
details.abstract: LLMs can engineer contexts via task-specific training, but no single method can achieve the best performance in all datasets at test time. Scaling helps but cannot reverse existing failures of LCEs. Even scaling to newer generations and more parameters remains insufficient to make LCEs more effective across different settings. When&How: Through aggregate analysis, we find that LCEs work better when facing less diverse failure modes of reasoning. title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability

details.title: Stable Gated DeltaNet-2: Understanding and Mitigating Recurrent State Instability
details.abstract: Linear attention offers an efficient solution for long-sequence modeling via linear complexity and fixed-size recurrent states. Gated DeltaNet-2 (GDN-2) introduces independent channel-wise control over erasure and writing, enhancing state-update expressiveness and in-context retrieval, yet it suffers from training failures during long-context training. We trace these failures to the asymmetry between reading and modification directions during erasure, which yields non-normal erase operators whose directional gains accumulate across tokens, triggering exponential state growth even without new writes. To resolve this, we propose Stable GDN-2, employing symmetric erasure to ensure non-expansive state propagation and decay-regulated residual writing to preserve writing flexibility. Theoretically, we establish an O(√T) upper bound on recurrent state growth while retaining chunkwise parallel computation. Experiments on ~1.6B parameter models show that Stable GDN-2 achieves stable training alongside improved long-context retrieval. Compared to GDN-2, it boosts the 128K average RULER score by 6.80 points in the recurrent setting and average accuracy across nine downstream tasks by 0.62 points in the hybrid setting.

title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models

details.title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
details.abstract: A foundation model for time series is pre-trained once and then asked to forecast series it has never seen, so the evidence for it is its score on held-out datasets. Such datasets are scarce, and a few public leaderboards carry most comparisons, yet none of them states how small a difference its datasets can detect. We call that quantity the resolution of a board and introduce Vernier , a tool that computes it from the files a board already publishes. Vernier also reports which entries a board cannot separate from its leader and whether its order changes when unrelated parties submit. GIFT-Eval resolves 6.8 rank places, and its displayed neighbours sit 0.91 apart. The ten places of its top ten hold fewer than two resolvable steps. fev-bench, Chronos Benchmark II and TIME show the same pattern: their resolution is 3.6 to 19 times the gap between neighbours. With each of its 2,554 series as an independent source, BOOM is the one board that resolves its top ten. Below the resolution the order depends on who else submitted: across four boards, rules that rank against the pool reversed 43 top-ten pairs with neither entry rerun, in one update in seven. Boards also do not record how much history a model receives. On 70 configurations, shortening it raised the error of three of four open models, two of them by 15%. title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation

details.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
details.abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text detail, and multimodal inputs. We evaluate five video generators using verified, case-specific checklists. Experiments show that proxies improve spatiotemporal control, but greater proxy detail can coincide with poorer completion, while strong structural adherence does not ensure correct binding.

title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation

details.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
details.abstract: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes. Confirmed generation results are linked to the corresponding asset states, story time, and reference versions for verification and reuse by subsequent shots. Hierarchical Collaboration isolates execution contexts by task, clip, and repair round, and uses hierarchical memory to organize this process across multiple sets. Across multiple benchmarks, StateWeaver outperforms existing methods and produces long videos with sustained cross-shot consistency under predefined and autonomously planned storyboards.

title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation

details.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
details.abstract: TL;DR: When a multimodal LLM agent calls a learned visuomotor policy (e.g., a VLA), the system often fails at the handoff : the agent invokes the policy from states where the policy is not reliable. We call the region where the policy is reliable its handoff boundary , and propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning . It shapes this boundary through training instead of leaving the agent to guess where it lies. Boundary-Explicit Training: fine-tune the policy only on contact segments, starting from diverse poses. This makes the boundary wide and simple enough to describe to the agent in a short handoff protocol. Boundary-Expanding Self-Improvement: curate the system's own successful rollouts and retrain the policy on them. This extends the boundary to earlier task stages, so the agent hands over sooner and makes fewer LLM calls. Results 98.4% success in randomized RoboTwin 2.0 scenes, +26.4 points over the strongest baseline; 69.2% on RoboDojo, +28.4 points. Self-improvement cuts API cost by 41.3% and execution time by 37.5% on average, with no drop in success. 91.1% of the agent's first handoffs land within 40 mm of the policy's training trajectories. title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?

details.title: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage?
details.abstract: We gave a minimal tool-calling agent database tasks with hazards in them (free up disk space, clean up tables, an instruction injected into the data, a superuser password left in an application table) and ran six small open-weight models against nine engines: PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, ClickHouse, Cassandra, MongoDB, Valkey, Kafka and OpenSearch. 9,468 trials, preregistered. Some results: Under least privilege, agents used the planted superuser password in 24 of 4,032 trials, all but one after the engine had refused their own account. Out of the box, in 215 of 392 trials that lost data, the only thing lost was a backup copy the agent could reach. The engine mattered most in what it lets you undo. Cassandra's default snapshot before TRUNCATE and DROP undid every such loss (0 of 432 trials). Model choice moved loss about as much as engine choice: 3.0% to 16.8% out of the box. Three of the seven preregistered hypotheses met their decision rule. Every trial record, with per-turn model reasoning, is on Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24445015

title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning

details.title: Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN): A Universal Primitive for Continuous-Time Spatiotemporal Learning
details.abstract: 👋 Hi everyone! Author here sharing Damped Atomic Wave Integration Neurons (DAWIN) — a solver-free, continuous-time neural primitive designed to replace standard perceptrons across MLPs, Transformers, and GNNs when modeling irregularly sampled spatiotemporal data. Key Motivation — Why DAWIN? Conventional neurons ( y = σ(wᵀx + b) ) decouple spatial feature aggregation from continuous physical time, forcing models on asynchronous event streams to rely on slow numerical ODE/CDE solvers or task-specific sequence wrappers. Atomic Spatiotemporal Wave Integration: Each DAWIN unit fuses spatial projection ( kₘᵀ xᵢ ) and Zero-Order Hold (ZOH) interval scaling ( αₘ(Δtᵢ) ) into an indivisible complex wave packet, integrating it directly into a local state governed by a continuous-time damper evolution operator exp(-(γₘ + iωₘ)Δtᵢ) . Provable Stability & Exact Generalization: Uniform Bounded-Input Bounded-Output (BIBO) stability holds for any damping rate γₘ > 0 without inner-loop normalization, while strictly generalizing static sinusoidal perceptrons ( γₘ → ∞ ) and memoryless wave neurons. Fused Triton Associative Scan ( O(log L) Parallel Depth): By proving exact associativity of atomic wave integration, our paired-real Triton prefix-scan kernel ( DAWINLinear ) eliminates serial recurrence bottlenecks with strict FP32 accumulation. Key 10-Seed Results (NVIDIA B200, Strict ±2% Parameter Parity) Clinical Time Series ( PhysioNet-12 ): DAWIN-Transformer achieves the best overall accuracy on dense clinical dynamics ( 0.9531 NRMSE , winning 10/10 seeds, Holm p = 0.010) and ties for top mortality prediction ( 0.9993 AUROC ). Cross-Task Accuracy & Causal Timing: Outperforms Neural CDE on 9/11 tasks and parameter-matched ReLU-MLP on 8/11 tasks. Shuffling elapsed intervals Δt degrades test error by +58.2% to +77.4% on physical dynamics tasks vs. +0.06% on a Δt -irrelevant control. Hardware Scaling: Accelerates inference by up to 2,630× over serial wave recurrence and 18.6×–802.3× over S5, Mamba, and Neural CDE, while reducing peak GPU VRAM by up to 97.6% . title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models

details.title: BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models
details.abstract: Hi everyone! We are excited to share BiSAT: Bidirectionally Aligned Semantic-Acoustic Tokenization for Speech Language Models ( arXiv:2611.30723 ). 🎧 Listen to Live Audio Demos: https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ (zero-shot TTS & speech reconstruction samples) 🚀 Open-Source Release Coming Soon: We are actively preparing the public release of both the source code and pretrained checkpoints for BiSAT ( BiSAT-32k , BiSAT-64k ) and BiSAT-TTS ( BiSAT-TTS-32k , BiSAT-TTS-64k ). Like seekmind-lab/bisat-paper or follow SeekMind Lab to be notified! Audio Demos (Live): https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ Blog Article (Full Walkthrough): https://huggingface.co/blog/zenkingsama/bisat Paper Companion & Release Tracker: https://huggingface.co/seekmind-lab/bisat-paper Organization: SeekMind Lab 1. Beyond Reconstruction: Why Code Structure Matters Evaluating discrete speech tokenizers by clean reconstruction WER alone can be misleading: X-Codec2 (50 Hz, 800 bps, adversarial waveform decoder) nearly matches BiSAT-32k (25 Hz, 375 bps, no adversarial training) on LibriSpeech-PC ( 2.27% vs. 2.15% WER ), yet degrades sharply on frozen-code understanding probes ( 8.82% vs. 1.92% PR PER , 87.7% vs. 24.4% zero-shot FLEURS EN WER , 5.6% vs. 40.4% VoxCeleb1 SID ). 2. How BiSAT Works: Separate Continuous Spaces, One Shared Index Inspired by TokenFlow's shared-index principle, BiSAT keeps acoustic (mel reconstruction without adversarial training) and semantic (CTC + layer-9 intermediate CTC) branches separate in continuous space , coupling them through a shared-index vector quantizer (SVQ) that selects one shared index per 25 Hz frame without a frozen semantic teacher. Two-stage training + spherical k-means initialization + rotation trick + shared-count EMA + dead-code reseeding yield 100% utilization at 32k ( 375 bps ) and 99.8% at 64k ( 400 bps ). 3. Inside the Paired Codebooks Joint training steadily reduces excess quantization distortion $r_b$ across both branches while maintaining asymmetric neighborhood correspondence well below the random baseline ($p = 0.005$). TreeSHAP attribution confirms clean branch specialization: Pitch ($F_0$, 80.8% ) and Energy ( 80.0% ) rely on $\boldsymbol{c}_a$, Phonemes ( 76.0% ) rely on $\boldsymbol{c}_s$, and Speaker ID ( 71.0% / 29.0% ) and Emotion ( 68.0% / 32.0% ) draw on both. 4. BiSAT-TTS: Zero-Shot TTS with 1/8th the Data of CosyVoice 3 Pairing a MiniCPM4-0.5B AR text-speech LM with a 22-block DiT conditional flow-matching acoustic decoder (supporting both offline and streaming decoding) trained on 122k hours across 11 languages, BiSAT-TTS achieves 1.50% WER on LibriSpeech-PC, 1.21% WER on Seed-TTS ( test-en ), and 1.27% CER on Seed-TTS ( test-zh ) with a 0.016% failure rate. 🎧 Hear the samples yourself: https://seekmind-lab.github.io/bisat-demo/ — we welcome any questions or feedback on the paper!
